title: Low Distraction — diagnostics event schema
description: One structured schema for every event the launcher records. Modelled on the shared ProGallery logging standard so app and web data can be joined. Bump schema_version on any breaking change. Version 1.1.0 adds the six severity levels (trace/debug/info/warn/error/fatal), a category on every event, and app_id in the envelope.

omitted.user_id: The app has no accounts and no sign-in, so there is no identifier to hash. Nothing is sent in its place.
omitted.request_id: There are no requests to correlate: the app makes no network calls. attempt_id links one user action to its outcome instead.
omitted.environment: release_channel carries the same meaning (production / beta) and is already present.

drop_off.when: The last event before the app leaves the foreground

permission_state_resolved.when: After checking whether a feature holds its permission

access_fix_requested.when: The user asks for a permission to be fixed or granted

access_fix_result.when: The fix attempt finishes — the outcome half of the pair above

media_query_result.when: After walking storage for a file search

app_list_loaded.when: The home list has been built

app_launch_requested.when: The user taps an app — the intent half of the launch pair

app_launch_result.when: The launch finishes: opened, cancelled at the pause, or failed

search_performed.when: A search runs. The query itself is never recorded

bubble_toggled.when: The assistive bubble is switched on or off

guide_step.when: A step of the first-run guide is shown

guide_finished.when: The guide is completed or skipped

tea_mode.when: The five-minute break starts or ends

error_state_shown.when: An error message is put in front of the user

anr.when: The main thread was blocked long enough to be felt

rage_tap.when: Three or more taps on the same thing inside two seconds

dead_click.when: A tap that changed nothing at all

permission_loop.when: The same permission fix is asked for three times in one session

back_button_spam.when: Three or more back presses inside two seconds

scroll_depth.when: A scrollable list reaches a new depth

time_to_first_value.when: From session start to the first meaningful action

file_index_rebuild.when: The background walk of storage finishes (or fails)

bubble_hidden.when: The bubble steps aside over a payment or government app

not_applicable.api_request: The app has no INTERNET permission, so it makes no network calls and can never log one.
not_applicable.session_replay_marker: No session replay is recorded anywhere in the app.
not_applicable.user_id: No accounts, so no identifier — not even a hashed one.
not_applicable.database: No database. Nothing is stored beyond SharedPreferences and one log file.
not_applicable.server: There is no server. The app is the whole product.
not_applicable.infrastructure: No servers, no deployment, no services to monitor.
not_applicable.distributed_tracing: One process on one device; there is no request to trace across services.
not_applicable.login: No accounts and no sign-in, so there are no login attempts to log.
not_applicable.analytics: Analytics are deliberately absent: no trackers, no telemetry, no upload. The Signals and Log health sections of the report are the local equivalent.

logged_on_purpose.package: The package name of an app the user opened (e.g. com.example.app). It is a public product identifier, not personal data, and a launch problem cannot be debugged without it. The user-visible label is never recorded.

redaction: anything shaped like an email becomes [email]
privacy.opt_out: Settings → Record diagnostics (on by default). While it is off nothing at all is written.
privacy.transport: There is no transport. The app cannot reach the network; a report leaves the phone only when the user exports, shares or mails it.
